sections.h2: Where is Blacksburg, VA, and what kind of town is it?
sections.html:
Blacksburg is an incorporated town in Montgomery County, in the New River Valley of southwest Virginia, at about 2,080 feet above sea level. It is the largest town in the state by population, with 44,826 residents in the 2020 census, and it sits on the Eastern Continental Divide.

The town is part of the Blacksburg-Christiansburg metropolitan area, which also includes Christiansburg, the city of Radford and all of Montgomery, Pulaski and Giles counties. Blacksburg is about 10 miles north of Christiansburg and the I-81 interchange, and the drive to Roanoke by way of US 460 and I-81 usually takes less than an hour.

Blacksburg is a college town in a very literal way. Virginia Tech dominates the local economy and the housing market, which makes the market here behave differently from most Virginia towns of its size.

sections.h2: How did Blacksburg grow, and why does that matter for old houses?
sections.html:
William Black laid out a 16-block grid in 1797, and the General Assembly established the town on January 13, 1798. The town was incorporated in 1871, and Virginia Agricultural and Mechanical College, now Virginia Tech, opened on October 2, 1872.

Growth stayed modest for most of the next century. The population was 3,358 in 1950 and 9,384 in 1970. Then the 1970s annexed Virginia Tech into the town, and the count jumped to 30,638 by 1980. The first large student apartment complex, Terrace View, opened in 1970, and the Foxridge apartments followed in the mid 1970s as part of the Hethwood development.

Houses near Main Street and College Avenue sit on the oldest part of the town plan, while Hethwood grew in the 1970s. The age of a house tells you a lot about which systems are original, which is why we ask for a build year and roof age at the start of every conversation.

sections.h2: What does Virginia Tech mean for selling a house in Blacksburg?
sections.html:
It means the buyer pool, the rental pool and the calendar are all tied to the university. Virginia Tech is the top employer in town at more than 5,000 employees, and the town's own financial report lists Moog above 1,000. HCA Montgomery Regional Hospital falls in the 500 to 999 range, and NRV Community Services, the Town of Blacksburg and EaglePicher Wolverine each fall in the 250 to 499 range.

The median age was 21.7 in 2020, and only 24.7 percent of households were married couples. About 30.9 percent were people living alone. That tells you a large share of local demand is for rentals, shared houses and small units, not family homes.

  • Rental houses: a house leased to students on a yearly cycle is easiest to sell when you can document the lease end date and show a clean walkthrough.
  • Owner-occupied houses: faculty, staff and research employees often buy near campus and the Virginia Tech Corporate Research Center, where Honeywell and a National Weather Service office are located.
  • Timing: a vacant house in July is easier to show than an occupied one in May during finals.

If your property is a rental with tenants whose lease runs past your preferred closing date, tell us. We can discuss buying with tenants in place or setting a closing after the lease ends.

sections.h2: What is the weather like in Blacksburg, and how does it affect a house?
sections.html:
Because of the elevation, Blacksburg has a cooler hot-summer humid continental climate that gets about 24.7 inches of snow in a typical season. NOAA normals show a January mean of 31.9 degrees Fahrenheit and a July mean of 71.7, with an average of only 5 days a year at 90 degrees or higher.

Annual precipitation is about 42.6 inches, and snow can fall from December through March. The practical effect on a house is roof load and heating cost. On February 13, 2010, after a snowstorm dropped about two feet, the gym roof of the former Blacksburg High School collapsed, and the building was later condemned. Most houses are built to local snow load standards, but flat or low-slope roofs on older additions are worth having checked.

  • Look at roof framing on porches and rear additions before listing.
  • Confirm that the furnace or heat pump runs in the cold months, not only in the fall.
  • Check that gutters and downspouts carry water away from foundations, since most months bring more than 2.8 inches of precipitation.

Winter weather also affects showing schedules, and a house that is easy to walk on a snowy day sells better.

sections.h2: How do people get around Blacksburg, and does it change house values?
sections.html:
Blacksburg Transit runs bus service mostly to and from the Virginia Tech campus, and since 2020 every passenger rides for free, with Virginia Tech subsidizing the service. BT began operating in 1983. A regional commuter route called the Smart Way Bus connects Virginia Tech, downtown Blacksburg, Christiansburg, the Roanoke-Blacksburg Regional Airport and Roanoke.

US 460 is the main road in and out, a four-lane highway linking I-81 at Christiansburg with I-77 in Princeton, West Virginia. The Huckleberry Trail, built on the old railbed, runs through town and is a selling point for houses nearby.

Walkability to campus, a BT stop, or the downtown core generally matters more to Blacksburg buyers than a big yard. If your house sits close to a bus line, put that in your listing or offer request. If it sits on a long drive outside the core, a cash buyer will weigh commute time as well.

sections.h2: Which schools and local services serve Blacksburg houses?
sections.html:
Montgomery County Public Schools run the public schools in Blacksburg, not the town itself. Blacksburg High School sits at 3401 Bruin Lane, in a building that opened for the fall 2013 semester, behind Blacksburg Middle School on Prices Fork Road. Kipps Elementary is at 2801 Prices Fork Road, and the town also has Margaret Beeks, Gilbert Linkous and Harding Avenue elementary schools.

The town government has a six-member council and a mayor, elected in November of odd-numbered years. Ask the town's planning and building staff before you rent the house, change its use or plan an addition. For real estate tax bills, ask the town and Montgomery County offices which of them bills your parcel.

sections.h2: What does a seller owe at settlement in Blacksburg?
sections.html:
In Virginia the seller normally pays a grantor's tax of 50 cents for each $500 of the price, and the contract can move some or all of that to the buyer. Half goes to the state and half to the locality, and the circuit court clerk will not record the deed until it is paid.

Real estate taxes are a lien that outranks every other lien, so the closing agent pays any unpaid balance from the seller's proceeds, and the current year's tax is split between buyer and seller by contract. You also have to hand the buyer the Virginia Real Estate Board's residential property disclosure statement. Among other items it tells the buyer you make no statement about historic district rules, flood hazard areas, wastewater systems such as septic tanks, radon, or proximity to a public use airport, and it urges the buyer to investigate.

That septic item matters if your house is not on public sewer. If it has a septic system, have records of pumping and any repairs ready. The statutes are at Virginia Code 58.1-802, 58.1-3340 and 55.1-703.

sections.h2: How can a Blacksburg owner sell quickly for cash?
sections.html:
A cash sale lets you skip the buyer's financing and appraisal steps, so you can often pick a closing date that fits your move or your tenants' lease. You send us the address and a few details about the house, we look it over, and we reply with a written offer you can accept or decline.

Sellers here often tell us about the same handful of situations: an investor who owns a student rental and wants out, a family handling an inherited house, an owner relocating for a job, or a house with deferred maintenance that is hard to show during the school year. We buy as-is, which means you do not have to paint, patch or clear out before closing day.

This is general information about Blacksburg and not legal or tax advice.

faqs.q: Is Blacksburg a city or a town?
faqs.a: Blacksburg is a town in Montgomery County, not an independent city. It is Virginia's largest town by population, so county offices and town offices both play a role in property matters.

faqs.q: How many people live in Blacksburg, VA?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 44,826 residents, and the median age was 21.7 years because of Virginia Tech.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Blacksburg house that has tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes. You can sell a rental with tenants in place, and the buyer takes over the lease terms, or you can set the closing for after the lease ends. Share the lease and deposit details early so the buyer can plan.

faqs.q: Does Blacksburg get a lot of snow?
faqs.a: Blacksburg averages about 24.7 inches of snow in a season, mostly from December through March, according to NOAA normals reported by Wikipedia. A February 2010 storm that dropped about two feet of snow caused the gym roof of the old Blacksburg High School to collapse.

faqs.q: Who pays the Virginia grantor's tax in a Blacksburg sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays it unless the contract says otherwise. The rate is 50 cents per $500 of the sale price under Virginia Code 58.1-802.

faqs.q: What if my Blacksburg house has a septic system?
faqs.a: Virginia's seller disclosure form tells buyers that the owner makes no statement about the type, size or upkeep of any wastewater system, and urges them to check. Keep pumping and repair records on hand, because buyers and inspectors ask for them.
